conventions.commits: Conventional Commits, GPG-signed and DCO signed-off: git commit -S --signoff (CONTRIBUTING.md:67-72). Example from the Swift addition: 'feat(core): add Swift language support with tree-sitter-swift handler (#1742)'.
conventions.testing: Inline #[cfg(test)] mod tests in each languages/<lang>.rs with a parse_<lang>(src) helper using Parser::set_language(&tree_sitter_x::LANGUAGE.into()).expect(...); element tests use tree_sitter::Query::new(...).expect('ELEMENT_QUERY must be valid') plus QueryCursor; defuse test uses SemanticExtractor::extract_def_use_for_file. Registry tests live in languages/mod.rs and lang.rs. Integration tests live in crates/aptu-coder/tests/ and use common::call_tool_raw. Swift has inline tests only; no CLI-level Swift test was found.
conventions.linting: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy -- -D warnings (CONTRIBUTING.md:17-18; CI uses --locked --profile ci per the issue); workspace lints: undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used and expect_used are deny (test code exempt via cfg_attr); must_use_candidate, redundant_clone, needless_pass_by_value, large_enum_variant are warn; cargo deny check advisories licenses bans; REUSE SPDX header on each new file.
conventions.error_handling: Query compile failures become ParserError::QueryError from build_compiled_queries (parser.rs ~159-170); unknown language names become ParserError::UnsupportedLanguage (parser.rs ~221-240); handlers return Option/Vec and never panic in non-test code; get_node_text in languages/mod.rs does bounds-checked slicing; the java.rs and swift.rs handlers use end_byte() <= source.len() checks.

patterns: Registry pattern: one match arm in get_language_info() plus one in get_ts_language() per language, both keyed by the same string (languages/mod.rs).
Five query consts per handler module: ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY (java.rs:4-37, swift.rs:6-38).

Captures are name-based: parser_elements.rs matches 'function', 'func_name'/'method_name', 'class', 'class_name'/'type_name', 'call', 'import_path', 'type_ref', and the prefixes 'write.', 'read.', 'writeread.'. A new handler must reuse these names or its data is dropped.

Inheritance handler signature ExtractInheritanceHandler = fn(&Node, &str) -> Vec<String> with strings like 'extends X' and 'implements X' (java.rs:131-165, swift.rs:49-75). Swift gates on kind; Java walks child_by_field_name('superclass') and ('interfaces').

Java-style DEFUSE: write captures prefixed write., read captures prefixed read.; parser_elements dedupes reads at offsets already recorded as writes (parser_elements.rs ~868-895), so write patterns must appear before the broad read pattern in the query.
Element capture with @class on interface/enum/trait nodes (java.rs ELEMENT_QUERY) so the inheritance handler also runs for them (parser_elements.rs 398-405).
Optional handler slots: extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver, find_receiver_type are Option and are None for languages without a consumer (python, typescript, markdown, css, yaml).
Lazy per-language query compilation keyed on supported_languages() (parser.rs 191-196, commit 4d714d9, issue #1777 per commit message).

related_issues.title: [FEATURE] Add PHP language support via tree-sitter-php grammar
related_issues.relevance: The task. Body has the full scope and acceptance criteria. Comments: none. Labels: enhancement, testing, feature, feat.

constraints: Process: the issue body says the maintainers are implementing this in-house and external pull requests will be closed. Treat this research as input to the maintainers, not as a contribution.

Registry gate: parser.rs QUERY_CACHE is built from supported_languages() and get_compiled_queries returns UnsupportedLanguage for any name not in it, so 'php' must be added to lang.rs supported_languages() as well as to get_language_info() and get_ts_language().

Grammar choice: tree-sitter-php exports LANGUAGE_PHP (accepts <?php and inline HTML/text nodes) and LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY (no HTML). The HTML-template acceptance criterion needs LANGUAGE_PHP, not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY.

Note on the premise: DEFUSE_QUERY is not required by the type system. LanguageInfo.defuse_query is Option<&'static str> (mod.rs:54-68) and fortran, markdown, css, yaml and html set it to None. It is required by this task's scope (the issue lists it among the five queries) and by behaviour: parser_elements.rs:850-852 returns an empty vec when compiled.defuse is None, so analyze_symbol def-use would be empty for PHP.

Dependency age: AGENTS.md says new Cargo.lock entries must be at least 7 days old; .github/scripts/check-package-age.sh enforces it against crates.io. tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 has a GitHub release dated 2026-11-19, about 9 days before this run. The crates.io publish date was not checked.

Version compatibility (inferred from manifests, not compiled): tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 depends on tree-sitter-language = 0.1 and dev-depends on tree-sitter = 0.27. The workspace pins tree-sitter = 0.27.1 and Cargo.lock has tree-sitter 0.27.2 and tree-sitter-language 0.1.9.

Import fidelity: extract_imports_from_node (parser_elements.rs 22+) has no namespace_use_declaration arm, so the fallback arm stores the full statement text as ImportInfo.module with empty items. A PHP IMPORT_QUERY alone yields 'use App\Models\User;' as text, not the parsed name. Structured use-items would need a core change in parser_elements.rs.

Scope: the issue excludes extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver, find_receiver_type, trait use resolution, properties, constants, attributes, namespace aliasing, and .phtml/.inc/.module/.php5. No tool-schema change.

Stale docs: README, the languages/mod.rs module doc (lines 3-6) and lib.rs:11 omit Swift; lang.rs supported_languages() omits css and yaml, which are registered in get_language_info(). Mention these in the PR only if they are touched.
Commits must be GPG-signed and DCO signed off; each new file needs an SPDX header (REUSE).
Tool access: gh worked for issue #1864 and the tree-sitter-php repo only. Other clouatre-labs issues returned 'outside the experiment's fence', so related issue titles are unverified.
test_coverage: Affected areas: (1) languages/mod.rs has test_get_language_info_known, test_get_language_info_unknown, test_get_ts_language_known/unknown and a table test test_get_language_info_covers_remaining_registered_languages (tuples of name, has_references, has_imports); a php row fits there. (2) lang.rs has test_language_for_extension_happy_path/edge_case, and a schemars-gated test test_supported_file_ext_pattern_covers_all_extension_map_entries that automatically checks every EXTENSION_MAP entry, so adding ('php','php') is covered by it. Swift is absent from the table test. (3) java.rs and swift.rs each have inline tests for query compile and match, extract_inheritance happy path and no-clause edge, and defuse write site. (4) parser.rs has lazy-compile tests (compile_count, at most one compile per language) and extract_calls tests. (5) crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/integration_tests.rs has extension tests for tsx, c and cpp (lines ~3141-3280). (6) crates/aptu-coder/tests/ has analyze_* integration tests using common::call_tool_raw; none covers Swift or CSS at the CLI level, so the PHP integration test would be the first of its kind for a recent language. Gap: no test in the repo covers a mixed HTML/PHP file, a use-import text fallback, or a grammar without an HTML arm.

approaches.name: A: Java-parity handler with LANGUAGE_PHP (recommended)
approaches.description: New languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class/interface/trait/enum), CALL_QUERY (function, member, nullsafe member and scoped calls), REFERENCE_QUERY (named_type), IMPORT_QUERY (namespace_use_declaration), DEFUSE_QUERY (simple_parameter, assignment, augmented assignment, update, variable reads), and extract_inheritance walking base_clause and class_interface_clause. Leave extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver and find_receiver_type as None. Grammar is LANGUAGE_PHP. Wire lang.rs (EXTENSION_MAP, supported_languages), languages/mod.rs (pub mod, two arms, tests), Cargo.toml x2, Cargo.lock, README, and one integration test file.
pros: Meets every acceptance criterion in the issue, including the DEFUSE_QUERY scope item and the mixed-HTML requirement
Follows the java.rs and swift.rs templates line for line, so the diff is easy to review
Stays inside the issue's excluded-scope list (no receiver handlers)
cons: Use imports are stored as full statement text (fallback arm), so the 'use imports' acceptance item is met only in a weak form
Five queries must each be verified against the grammar; node-types were checked from the repo but the crate was not compiled in this run
Changes shared registry files used by every language

approaches.name: B: Minimal grammar-only integration
approaches.description: Same registry wiring as A, but ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY and extract_inheritance only. REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY and DEFUSE_QUERY are None, so the handler has no imports or def-use.
pros: Smallest query surface and the lowest chance of a query compile error
Fastest to a working analyze_file result for functions, classes and calls
cons: Fails the issue's 'use imports' and DEFUSE acceptance criteria as written, so the maintainers would have to send it back
analyze_symbol def-use returns empty for PHP (parser_elements.rs 850-852)
Leaves the registry looking inconsistent with java.rs and swift.rs

approaches.name: C: Java-parity plus structured use-imports in core
approaches.description: Approach A plus a new arm in parser_elements.rs extract_imports_from_node for namespace_use_declaration that splits namespace_use_clause children into ImportInfo items with aliases, and optional receiver handlers (extract_function_name, find_receiver_type) on php.rs.
pros: Gives real import items instead of statement text
Receiver handlers would match Java and Kotlin shape
cons: Receiver handlers are explicitly out of scope and have no consumer since #1807 (per the issue)
Touches the shared parser_elements.rs path used by all languages, which needs wider regression testing
The issue says to modify only files in scope; this exceeds it

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that meets the issue's acceptance criteria without touching shared core code or exceeding scope. Use LANGUAGE_PHP so the HTML-template criterion holds. Add 'php' to supported_languages() as well as the two registry match arms, or get_compiled_queries returns UnsupportedLanguage. Keep DEFUSE_QUERY because the issue scopes it and without it PHP def-use is empty. Accept the statement-text import fallback for now and log structured use-imports as a follow-up that touches parser_elements.rs. Verify every query with a compile test before wiring (the issue's step 3), and confirm the node kinds with a parse dump, which was not possible in this read-only run.

inheritance_walk_citation: Grammar source inspected: tree-sitter-php repo, php/grammar.js (a 102-byte wrapper calling defineGrammar('php') from common/define-grammar.js) and common/define-grammar.js lines 334-337, 365-373, 381-384. Verbatim rules: base_clause: $ => seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name)); class_declaration: $ => prec.right(seq(optional(field('attributes', $.attribute_list)), repeat($._modifier), keyword('class'), field('name', reserved('classes', $.name)), optional($.base_clause), optional($.class_interface_clause), field('body', $.declaration_list))); class_interface_clause: $ => seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name)); _name: $ => choice(alias(keyword('static', false), $.name), ..., reserved('classes', $.name), $.qualified_name, $.relative_name). node-types.json (php/src/node-types.json) confirms class_declaration.fields = {attributes, body, name} only, so neither clause is a field, and class_declaration.children.types includes 'base_clause' and 'class_interface_clause'. Field-by-field walk: (1) start at the class_declaration node (kind 'class_declaration'); (2) do NOT use child_by_field_name for inheritance; iterate node.children() by kind; (3) for the child of kind 'base_clause' (the extends clause, keyword token 'extends' is anonymous), iterate its named_children, keep kinds 'name', 'qualified_name', 'relative_name', and push format!('extends {text}') using the raw source slice; (4) for the child of kind 'class_interface_clause' (implements), iterate named_children with the same three kinds and push format!('implements {text}'); (5) return the Vec in source order. The same walk works for interface_declaration (its extends list is also a base_clause, so entries are 'extends X') and enum_declaration (which may carry only a class_interface_clause). tags.scm (queries/tags.scm) corroborates: (class_interface_clause [(name) (qualified_name)] @name) @reference.implementation.
